analysis:
Reviewed all 18 units. Changes are documentation, comment, and tooling edits. They are consistent with the console-ui move to the platform repo (the threat model scope already says console and backend are out of scope).

1. docs/reference/provider-authorization.md (head lines 3, 62-65) and docs/reference/telemetry-schema.md (head lines 3, 14-18, 108): console-ui references now point to immutable darkbloom-platform links at commit 48a198c7. The authorization semantics are unchanged. The TB-011 and T-052..T-058 statements about App Attest grants, receipt monitoring, removal readiness and the snapshotMaxAge=10 window are untouched. The telemetry text still says the client facade is inert and there is no ingestion route, so no new data-exposure surface appears. The Go/TypeScript mirrors are reclassified as external contracts that local checks do not execute, which is accurate and does not overclaim.

2. provider-swift/Tests/.../TelemetrySymmetryTests.swift (head lines 9-10): comment-only change. Test logic is unchanged.

3. mise.toml line 2: comment-only change. It now mentions a desktop app (Electron) that the supplied evidence does not show. This is not security-relevant.

4. infra/threat-review/merge-rules.json: removes the required status check 'Console UI Lint & Build' (base lines 80-83). The threat-model-review workflow rule and all provider, coordinator, docs, release-integrity and signature checks remain required. A check for a component that has left the repo is not a provider-side security control. Residual question for integration: whether the workflow that produced 'Console UI Lint & Build' was actually removed in this PR. If it still exists, dropping the required check would reduce CI gating. That workflow is not in the supplied evidence. Deleting a required check for a removed job also avoids blocking merges, so this is not a finding.

No threat IDs are affected and no regressions were identified.
